title: Reflection and refraction; Mirrors
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W14-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W04-ap1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W04-ap1#t4 term and clue written for the game; W04-ap1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W04-ap1#N.1, W14-1#N.4, W04-ap1#N.9, W14-1#N.9.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Concave mirror
items.clue: Converging reflector whose surface curves inwards, like the inside of a spoon.

items.label: Geometric optics
items.clue: Straight-line model of light, valid when objects and openings are much wider than λ.

items.label: Diffuse reflection
items.clue: Bouncing of light from a rough surface such as paper: parallel in, many directions out.

items.label: Ray diagram
items.clue: Drawing of the path of light before and after it meets matter, with arrows from the source.

questions.stem: A narrow laser beam passes through a very narrow slit and then spreads out, making a band of light on a distant screen far wider than the slit. Which explanation of this observation is correct?

options.text: The wave nature of light matters here, and a ray model cannot account for the spreading.
Rays from the slit's two edges fan out along straight lines toward the screen.
Light waves reflect off the edges of the slit, which sends them out to the sides.
Only a few rays can fit through the slit, and they move apart as they travel.

questions.stem: A convex mirror bulges towards the light. Predict before the next screen. A beam of light rays traveling parallel to the principal axis of a convex mirror strikes the mirror. Which statement describes the reflected rays?

options.text: They converge to a point in front of the mirror, where they cross.
They pass through a point behind the mirror, where they cross.
They diverge as if they came from a point behind the mirror.
They go back along their own paths, staying parallel to the axis.

questions.stem: A short pulse of light crosses a glass plate (n = 1.50) along the normal to its faces in a time t. The pulse then crosses a diamond plate (n = 2.42) that is twice as thick as the glass plate, also along the normal. How long does the pulse take to cross the diamond plate?
A student walks toward a tall plane mirror, from 3.0 m away to 1.0 m away. How does the height of the student's image at 1.0 m compare with its height at 3.0 m?

options.text: It is greater at 1.0 m, as the image looks bigger from closer up.
It is smaller at 1.0 m, as less of the student fits in the mirror.
Neither has a definite height, as a virtual image is not really there.
They are equal: the image is always as tall as the student.
